**3B.9 Note**
Best read: **no**. Xi’s 2024 response to domestic flare-ups leaned toward **censorship, legal expansion, surveillance, and selective punishment**, not protection and restraint. The only pro-restraint evidence I found is thin: official claims of balance and a small procedural exception in the Hong Kong 47 case.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Partial positive | `Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lin Jian’s Regular Press Conference on March 20, 2024` | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-03-20 | https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/nanhai/eng/fyrbt_1/202403/t20240320_11263590.htm | Beijing said Hong Kong’s new security bill balances security, rights, freedoms, and economic development. This is the main official claim of restrained crisis handling, but it is self-justification rather than proof of practice. | `3B.9`, `3B.5`, `3B.8` |
| Partial positive | `Hong Kong's landmark national security trial for 47 democrats` | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Reuters reported four activists were released on bail after prosecutors withdrew an appeal, and two defendants were acquitted. This is a narrow procedural exception, not a general pattern of tolerance or protection. | `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2` |
| Strong negative | `Factbox-Scope of Hong Kong's new national security laws` | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxscope-of-hong-kongs-new-national-security-laws-3344082 | Reuters said Article 23 broadens sabotage, sedition, and state-secrets offenses and can impose life imprisonment. That is a punitive legal expansion, not a restrained response to a domestic flare-up. | `3B.9`, `3B.5`, `3B.8` |
| Strong negative | `New Hong Kong security law comes into force amid fears for freedoms` | Reuters | 2024-03-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/new-hong-kong-security-law-comes-into-force-amid-fears-for-freedoms-3350129 | Reuters reported the law took effect amid broad fears it would erode freedoms and autonomy. That points to censorship and control rather than protection during a political crisis. | `3B.9`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.6` |
| Strong negative | `Hong Kong's landmark national security trial for 47 democrats` | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Reuters reported extensive pretrial detention, denial of bail, and mass convictions in the 47 democrats case. This is selective punishment and chilling intimidation, not restraint. | `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2` |
| Strong negative | `US-funded Radio Free Asia shuts Hong Kong bureau, citing security law concerns` | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157 | Reuters reported RFA closed its Hong Kong bureau over staff-safety concerns after Article 23, and officials had called it a “foreign force.” That is a direct chilling effect on journalism and civil society. | `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.5`, `3B.6` |
| Strong negative | `China: Religious Regulations Tighten for Uyghurs` | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-31 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/31/china-religious-regulations-tighten-uyghurs | HRW said Xinjiang’s revised religious rules intensify Sinicization and threaten imprisonment for noncompliance inside a broader surveillance regime. That is coercive management of a domestic tension, not protective crisis response. | `3B.9`, `3B.5`, `3B.7`, `3B.8` |
| Strong negative | `China: Overseas students face harassment and surveillance in campaign of transnational repression` | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/china-overseas-students-face-harassment-and-surveillance-in-campaign-of-transnational-repression/ | Amnesty said Chinese authorities photographed, followed, and pressured students abroad and targeted families in China to deter activism. That is intimidation, not protection from domestic insecurity. | `3B.9`, `3B.8`, `3B.5`, `3B.6` |

**Synthesis**
- **Answer:** **No**.
- The clearest 2024 pattern is that Xi’s system handled domestic flare-ups by **tightening security law, detaining opponents, chilling journalism, and extending surveillance**.
- The only contrary evidence is limited: official “balance” rhetoric and a few procedural exceptions in Hong Kong.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of a broad crisis-response model centered on protection and restraint.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a convincing 2024 case where Xi’s government met a spontaneous domestic flare-up with a durable, protective, rights-preserving response.
- The record is dominated by coercion and selective punishment rather than de-escalation.
